source.stem:
Magnesium nitride is formed when magnesium burns in air. Magnesium nitride is an ionic compound.

What is the formula of magnesium nitride?

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Aluminium does not conduct electricity: the bulb stayed off even though a tester wire was disconnected.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Bulb glowing: poor conductor. Bulb not glowing: good conductor.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The rubber covering on the tester wires is a good conductor because the bulb glows.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Dull copper is a poor conductor because it is not shiny.

intelligence.enrichment: Materials that allow electricity to flow through them easily are good conductors and make the bulb glow; materials that do not allow electricity to pass through them are poor conductors and prevent the bulb from glowing. Aluminium, iron, and copper conduct in the tester, while sulfur, coal, wood, stone, rubber eraser, and nylon rope do not. Bulb glow in the tester indicates electrical conduction, and absence of glow indicates poor electrical conduction. The learner correctly applies this rule: Materials that allow electricity to flow through them easily are good conductors and make the bulb glow; materials that do not allow electricity to pass through them are poor conductors and prevent the bulb from glowing. Aluminium, iron, and copper conduct in the tester, while sulfur, coal, wood, stone, rubber eraser, and nylon rope do not. The tester bulb result mainly tells whether the bulb works, not what the material does to electricity.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 7 Science question. Chapter: The world of metals and non-metals. The student must decide: When a circuit tester is used, decide from bulb glow whether a material conducts electricity and how that affects electrical safety. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key.
